# Independent review plan for P1

Date: 2026-10-23.
Reviewer: Codex subagent `p1_independent`.
This is an AI review simulation.
It does not provide human scientific endorsement.

The reviewer read the approved scope, W013 proposal, task templates, review template, and collaboration rules before preparing this plan.
The reviewer did not inspect the new example code or its outputs before fixing these criteria.
The user approved one synthetic example with two fixed datasets.
The reviewer can run one independent replay after the coordinator supplies a sealed result.

## Fixed review criteria

1. Make sure that the reference uses exact rational values of the actual binary inputs.
   Inspect all 24 results for both methods and all six permutations of each dataset.
   Derive expected values independently from the fixed inputs and binary64 rounding.
   Preserve float identities and exact errors.
2. Make sure that the report retains ties and contrary evidence.
   The exact control has six ties.
   The cancellation case has two ties and four cases with different errors under ordinary binary64 rounding.
   Do not require a favorable method result for task acceptance.
3. Make sure that records distinguish actual execution from plans and API documentation.
   Inspect the execution command, exit status, actual Python version, elapsed time, and recorded output.
   Treat unavailable assistant usage as unknown.
   Do not infer an execution from a plausible output alone.
4. Make sure that the submitted contract, inputs, result, and artifacts match their recorded SHA256 digests.
   Run exactly one full replay with a 30-second timeout in a fresh temporary directory.
   Compare numerical content and measure sealed-file digests before and after replay.
   Do not edit sealed files or use their output path for replay.
5. Make sure that source notes identify the sections actually read and their limits.
   Distinguish official API documentation from a literature review or experiment evidence.
   Make sure that claims cite actual output rows and retain the platform and input limits.
   Reject claims of novelty, general superiority, speed, significance, or measured multi-agent benefit.
6. Make sure that the task has one named acceptance owner and a separate review record.
   Inspect the current and fixed contracts, review history, task scope, final state, and active-job facts.
   Run the existing record checker on the complete selected records.
   Accept only the exact result that satisfies every required condition.

## Independent numerical basis

The exact control contains the binary integers 1, 2, and 3.
Every intermediate sum remains an exactly representable integer, so all 12 outputs equal 6 with zero error.
The cancellation inputs are the exactly representable binary integers 10000000000000000, 1, and -10000000000000000.
Their exact rational sum equals 1.
The spacing around either large magnitude is 2.
Adding 1 first to either large magnitude rounds to that large value under ties-to-even rounding.
Those four accumulation orders return 0 with absolute error 1.
The two orders that add opposite large values first return 1 with zero error.
Accurate summation returns 1 for all six cancellation orders on the declared platform.
The reviewer will compare these expectations with the actual output and report any difference rather than change the criteria.

## Evidence and limits

Save the replay command, return code, output, duration, numerical comparisons, and file digests under this review directory.
Write the final review only after the contract assigns its decision owner.
Keep the final review separate from the sealed attempt.
Do not run a new method comparison, P2 recovery test, or P3 collaboration trial.
This review does not establish a benefit for real research or cross-harness recovery.
limits: No original research, statistical significance, speed comparison, or multi-agent benefit claim.
No DSH, restart, cross-harness recovery, or external job test.
No portable skill or package version change.

baseline_proposal:
# W013: Propose a complete synthetic example

Status: captured.
Package version: `0.1.6`, unchanged.
Date: 2026-10-23.

The user asked to continue improvements after N6.
The original request requires review and approval for each improvement.
This record proposes P1 for approval.
It does not authorize implementation or an experiment run.
No example directory, measured result, or active research rule exists from this proposal.

## Proposed scope

Create one synthetic computational practice example in `examples/summation-order/`.
The question is how input order affects floating-point summation error on two fixed datasets.
Compare an explicit accumulation loop with `math.fsum`.
Calculate the reference sum from `Fraction.from_float` values for the actual binary inputs.
The example demonstrates traceable execution and review, with no claim of research novelty or general method superiority.

The official [math.fsum documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/math.html#math.fsum) describes accurate summation and platform-dependent rounding limits.
The official [Fraction documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/fractions.html#fractions.Fraction.from_float) distinguishes binary float values from decimal fractions.
These sections were inspected on 2026-10-23.
They are API documentation, not a literature review or evidence of an executed experiment.
The implementation must record its actual Python version separately from the documentation version.

Use one execution task and a separate AI review.
The coordinator alone writes shared state and the current task contract.
The worker owns only the assigned attempt outputs.
The existing collaboration procedure remains the authority for acceptance.
Label the review as AI simulation.

## Fixed candidate protocol

Use these two synthetic datasets:

| Case | Input values | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact control | `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` | Retain a case where the methods can tie. |
| Cancellation | `[1e16, 1.0, -1e16]` | Inspect order effects with unequal magnitudes. |

Evaluate all six permutations of each dataset with both methods.
Use a plain loop for the baseline, without substituting the built-in `sum` implementation.
Record each input order, each method output, and exact absolute error against the binary-input reference.
Store float identities and rational errors without rounding away differences.
Freeze the protocol, inputs, and code hashes before the measured run.
Keep ties, failed attempts, and contradictory results.
Do not require a favorable result for `math.fsum` to accept an accurate report.
Do not report speed, statistical significance, or a multi-agent benefit from this example.

The proposed budget is one candidate within 60 minutes after approval.
Use the existing local Python environment and the standard library.
Allow one measured run and one independent replay, each with a 30-second timeout.
Allow one repair cycle with the same two-run limit, while preserving failed attempts.
Use temporary directories for execution and replay before saving the approved example artifacts.
Use no GPU, paid API, account connection, dataset download, or new dependency.
Record unavailable assistant usage measurements as unknown.
Stop when the example passes review or reaches these limits.

## Proposed files and acceptance

The example contains a README report, brief, state, source notes, claims, one question, and one experiment record.
It contains one current task contract, its fixed attempt copy, a result record, and one separate review.
Attempt artifacts contain the script, inputs, actual results, and execution log.
New attempts preserve old attempts when repairs are necessary.
Replay writes to a new temporary path and cannot overwrite the sealed example.

Allowed implementation paths are `examples/summation-order/`, both root README files, and `tests/test_package.py`.
Also allow one focused example test at `tests/test_summation_example.py`.
Record the decision in this file, `tests/RESULTS.md`, and `tests/evidence/W013.json`.
Add `examples` to the existing package link checks because they currently omit that directory.
Keep the portable skill, record schemas, dependencies, CI workflow, and N6 changes unchanged.

Acceptance requires actual output for every declared case and method.
Each reported observation must link to its output rows.
A separate reviewer must inspect the protocol, code, outputs, and claims.
The record checker must accept the selected contract, result, and completed review.
A clean replay must reproduce the numerical results without changing sealed files.
The focused example test and existing offline suite must pass.
The final state must identify current evidence, remaining limits, and no active job after local execution ends.
Failed execution or unavailable access must remain a recorded limit rather than a fabricated result.

## Decision and recovery

Decision: Awaiting user approval of the example topic, files, and budget.
An independent scope review found this example suitable and identified the missing link-check coverage for `examples/`.
No numerical experiment, cross-harness recovery test, or collaboration performance comparison ran.
P2 can later add a frozen handoff and a separately approved recovery test using the saved P1 records.
P3 can later compare execution strategies under a separate fixed budget.
P1 does not authorize either trial or a runtime framework change.
Rejecting this proposal leaves the current workflow unchanged.

+"""Check the synthetic example without replacing its saved experiment outputs."""
+
+import copy
+from fractions import Fraction
+import hashlib
+from itertools import permutations
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import types
+import unittest
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+EXAMPLE = ROOT / "examples/summation-order"
+ARTIFACTS = EXAMPLE / "tasks/T001/attempts/A001/artifacts"
+EXPERIMENT = types.ModuleType("summation_example")
+SCRIPT = ARTIFACTS / "run.py"
+# Keep bytecode caches out of the sealed attempt, including under other test runners.
+exec(compile(SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(SCRIPT), "exec"), EXPERIMENT.__dict__)
+
+
+class SummationExampleTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_binary_reference_and_all_input_orders(self):
+        values = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
+        data = {"protocol_version": "1", "cases": [{"id": "decimal-control", "values": values}]}
+        before = copy.deepcopy(data)
+        rows = EXPERIMENT.evaluate(data)["rows"]
+        self.assertEqual(data, before)
+        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 6)
+        self.assertEqual({tuple(row["input_hex"]) for row in rows},
+                         {tuple(value.hex() for value in order) for order in permutations(values)})
+        reference = Fraction(0.1) + Fraction(0.2) + Fraction(0.3)
+        self.assertNotEqual(reference, Fraction(3, 5), "The reference must use actual binary inputs.")
+        for row in rows:
+            self.assertEqual(Fraction(**row["reference"]), reference)
+            self.assertEqual(set(row["methods"]), {"naive", "fsum"})
+            for output in row["methods"].values():
+                exact_output = Fraction(float.fromhex(output["value_hex"]))
+                self.assertEqual(Fraction(**output["absolute_error"]), abs(exact_output - reference))
+
+    def test_invalid_input_fails_before_output(self):
+        valid = {"protocol_version": "1", "cases": [{"id": "small", "values": [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]}]}
+        invalid = [None, {**valid, "protocol_version": "2"}, {**valid, "cases": []}]
+        for values in ([True, 0.5, 0.75], [float("nan"), 0.5, 0.75], [float("inf"), 0.5, 0.75],
+                       [0.25, 0.25, 0.75], [0.25, 0.5], ["0.25", 0.5, 0.75]):
+            invalid.append({**valid, "cases": [{"id": "small", "values": values}]})
+        invalid.append({**valid, "cases": valid["cases"] * 2})
+        for data in invalid:
+            with self.subTest(data=data), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                EXPERIMENT.evaluate(data)
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
+            path = Path(temp) / "invalid.json"
+            path.write_text('{"protocol_version":"1","cases":[]}', encoding="utf-8")
+            result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(ARTIFACTS / "run.py"), str(path)],
+                                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn("nonempty list", result.stderr)
+        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", result.stderr)
+
+    def test_saved_result_and_review_remain_bound(self):
+        before = {str(p.relative_to(EXAMPLE)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+                  for p in EXAMPLE.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
+        loaded = subprocess.run(
+            [sys.executable, "-c", "import runpy, sys\nrunpy.run_path(sys.argv[1], run_name='loader_probe')", __file__],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(loaded.returncode, 0, loaded.stdout + loaded.stderr)
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            [sys.executable, "-B", str(ROOT / "skills/research-workflow/scripts/lint_records.py"),
+             "--root", str(EXAMPLE), "--task", "tasks/T001/task.json",
+             "--result", "tasks/T001/attempts/A001/result.json", "--review", "reviews/R001.md"],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout), {"diagnostics": []})
+        after = {str(p.relative_to(EXAMPLE)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+                 for p in EXAMPLE.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
+        self.assertEqual(after, before)
+        rows = json.loads((ARTIFACTS / "results.json").read_text())["rows"]
+        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 12)
+        self.assertEqual({(row["case_id"], row["order_index"]) for row in rows},
+                         {(case, index) for case in ("control", "cancellation") for index in range(1, 7)})
+        ties = 0
+        for row in rows:
+            self.assertEqual(set(row["methods"]), {"naive", "fsum"})
+            errors = [Fraction(**entry["absolute_error"]) for entry in row["methods"].values()]
+            ties += errors[0] == errors[1]
+        self.assertEqual(ties, 8, "Keep the stored ties as part of the reported result.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
